en.title: McDavid's 21-game streak meets a Flyers team the model rates higher than the market
en.deck: Edmonton has won four straight, the latest a 1-0 win in Toronto on Devon Levi's first NHL shutout, and Connor McDavid has a point in all 21 games. Philadelphia won 4-3 in Columbus on Saturday, so both teams play the second night of a back-to-back, four days after the Oilers won 3-2 in overtime in Edmonton. The market makes Edmonton a clear favourite; the model leans the other way.
news: Levi made 19 saves in Toronto. Edmonton has not named Sunday's starter, and the site lists Tristan Jarry as the likely goalie. Dan Vladar is confirmed for Philadelphia.
Mike Babcock's Oilers are 15-3-3 and 10-2-2 in their past 14. Frederik Andersen (knee), Matt Savoie, Mattias Janmark and Isaac Howard are on injured reserve.
Denver Barkey scored twice in Columbus, including the winner, for his first multi-goal NHL game. Matvei Michkov scored his 11th goal on a breakaway, and Trevor Zegras ended a seven-game goal drought.
Rick Tocchet's Flyers finished their five-game road trip 2-1-2 and have points in three straight.
records: McDavid has 50 points (11 goals, 39 assists) and is the fifth player to reach 50 points in 21 games or fewer, after Wayne Gretzky, Mario Lemieux, Bernie Nicholls and Mike Bossy.
Evan Bouchard leads all NHL defencemen with 34 points. He has 367 career points, one behind Charlie Huddy (368) for third among Oilers defencemen.
Leon Draisaitl has an eight-game point streak, the 20th streak of eight games or more in his career.
Philadelphia (6-10-6) has six losses after regulation and scores 2.24 goals a game. The model flags Michkov's finishing as running hot.
betting: Market: Oilers 1.61, Flyers 2.38, about 60–40 without the margin. The model has it 53–47 for Philadelphia, the biggest moneyline gap on Sunday. It notes that Edmonton has had only 48% of the expected goals at 5-on-5 while its shooting and goaltending run well above normal.
Total: over 5.5 at 1.64 is about 58%; the model says 53%. The last seven meetings averaged 6.1 goals.

Player chances (model): McDavid 1+ point 79% (market about 80%), Bouchard 1+ point 61% (about 66%), Zegras 1+ point 54% (about 53%). McDavid to score is 35% in the model against 2.23 in the market (45% with the margin).

Philadelphia vann 4–3 i Columbus på lördagen, så båda lagen spelar andra kvällen i rad, fyra dagar efter Oilers 3–2-seger på övertid i Edmonton. Marknaden ser Edmonton som klar favorit, modellen lutar åt andra hållet.

Rick Tocchets Flyers avslutade bortaturnén på fem matcher med 2-1-2 och har tagit poäng i tre raka.

en.title: Benn's 1,000th point behind them, the Stars meet a Panthers team still missing Barkov
en.deck: Jamie Benn reached 1,000 points in Saturday's 2-0 win over Buffalo, and Jake Oettinger got his league-leading fourth shutout. Florida has won three straight, the last 4-1 in St. Louis, but Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand are still out. Both teams are on a back-to-back, and the model and the market almost agree.
news: Miro Heiskanen practised Saturday but is doubtful and would miss a fifth straight game. Dallas also has Lian Bichsel and Kyle Capobianco on injured reserve.
Barkov (knee, hurt Oct. 1) and Marchand (lower body, Oct. 6) are travelling with the Panthers on the road trip. On Nov. 10, Paul Maurice said both were within two weeks of a return.
Brady Tkachuk had a power-play goal and an assist in St. Louis and has eight points in his past seven games. Jacob Markstrom made 23 saves; the site expects Akira Schmid on Sunday.
Dallas has not named its starter after Oettinger's 22-save shutout.
records: Benn, 37, is the 104th player with 1,000 NHL points and the second in Stars/North Stars history after Mike Modano (1,359).
Oettinger's shutout was the 20th of his career.
Matthew Tkachuk has assists in seven straight games (nine in all) and needs one point for 700 in his career.
Only 6 of Dallas' 19 games have gone over 5.5 goals, but the last six meetings averaged 7.2.
betting: Market: Stars 1.75, Panthers 2.12, about 55–45 without the margin. The model says 56–44, so they agree.
Total: over 5.5 at 1.76 is about 54%; the model says 56%. Dallas' low-scoring season pulls one way, the high-scoring head-to-head history the other.

en.title: Gauthier takes an eight-game goal streak into the Ducks' rematch with Calgary
en.deck: Cutter Gauthier has 15 goals during an eight-game goal streak, three games from Teemu Selanne's franchise record of 11. The Ducks have lost two straight since a five-game winning streak, the latest 6-2 to the Islanders, while Calgary won 3-2 in Los Angeles on Saturday and can get back to .500. The market expects more goals than the model does.
news: Lukas Dostal allowed six goals on 25 shots on Saturday in his first start in over a week; he had been pulled after one period in Calgary on Nov. 6. Laurent Brossoit was sent to AHL San Diego.
Dustin Wolf made 29 saves in Los Angeles. The site lists Devin Cooley as the likely starter on the second night of the back-to-back.
Calgary is without Jonathan Huberdeau (hip), who did not travel, and Kevin Bahl, who is out for the season after Achilles surgery.
Joel Quenneville's Ducks finish a four-game homestand here, then start a four-game road trip in St. Louis on Tuesday.
records: Gauthier's streak ties Selanne's 1998-99 run for the second-longest in Ducks history. Selanne scored in 11 straight in 1997-98.
Anaheim scores 3.74 goals a game and has the league's top power play (36.8%), but allows 3.68 a game, 30th in the NHL. 17 of its 20 games have gone over 5.5.
Yegor Sharangovich has five points (1 goal, 4 assists) in a three-game point streak.
The Ducks lead the season series 2-1, and this is the last of four meetings.
betting: Market: Ducks 1.64, Flames 2.32, about 59–41 without the margin. The model says 56–44, a little warmer on Calgary.
Total: over 5.5 at 1.48 is about 64% and over 6.5 at 1.76 about 54%. The model says 58% and 48%, so the market is higher on goals, even with the Ducks' over-heavy season.

Player chances (model): Mikael Granlund 1+ point 63% (market about 60%), Jackson LaCombe 1+ point 60% (about 61%), Joel Farabee goal 28% (2.95, 34% with the margin). The model flags Gauthier's finishing as running hot.

en.title: The Canucks carry a seven-game skid into Vegas
en.deck: Vancouver is 3-17-1 and has won once in 18 games since a 2-1 start, and it is last in the NHL in points and in goals allowed (4.52 a game). Vegas had won four straight before Friday's shootout loss to Nashville. The market gives the Canucks about one chance in five; the model gives them closer to one in three.
news: First-year coach Manny Malhotra said after Friday's 5-1 loss to the Rangers that his team too often "goes off script and cracks" in big moments. Sunday opens a three-game road trip.
Leevi Merilainen is the likely Vancouver starter. Thatcher Demko is out after hip surgery, and Henrik Sedin has said he hopes Demko is back before Christmas.
Adin Hill made 30 saves on Friday. Ryan Craig said Vegas lost its puck management in the third period. Noah Hanifin is out for Vegas.
records: Brock Boeser reached 500 career points in his 650th game on Friday, the eighth player in Canucks history to do it, and has a six-game point streak.
Mitch Marner has a 10-game home point streak, the fourth Golden Knight to manage one after Mark Stone, Reilly Smith and Jack Eichel.
Vancouver has allowed five or more goals in 10 of its 21 games.
Vegas won the first meeting 3-2 in Vancouver on Oct. 4, and the last 12 meetings averaged only 5.3 goals.
betting: Market: Golden Knights 1.21, Canucks 4.60, about 79–21 without the margin. The model says 68–32 and gives Vancouver clearly more of a chance than the market does.

en.title: Rested Predators chase an eighth straight win against tired Sharks
en.deck: Nashville has won seven in a row, tying Carolina for the longest winning streak this season, and has had a day off since Friday's shootout win in Vegas. San Jose plays the second night of a back-to-back after rallying from two goals down to beat Utah 6-5 in a shootout. The market likes Nashville more than the model does.
news: Juuse Saros made 40 saves in Vegas and was named the NHL's third star of the week. The site lists Justus Annunen as the likely starter on Sunday.
Coach Andrew Brunette credited the streak to everybody chipping in. Jonathan Marchessault is day-to-day with a lower-body injury.
Yaroslav Askarov made 27 saves in Utah, where Dmitry Orlov had four points and Eric Pohlkamp scored his first NHL goal. The site expects Alex Nedeljkovic in net.
San Jose is without Alexander Wennberg and Igor Chernyshov, and had lost six of seven before Saturday.
records: Roman Josi has 23 points (2 goals, 21 assists) and is the first Predator with 21 assists in his team's first 20 games.
Ryan O'Reilly scored twice in Vegas for nine goals this season.
Nashville has won four straight on the road, and it entered Friday with the league's second-best penalty kill (89.5%).
The last 10 meetings averaged 7.8 goals.
